title: applyLifecycle writes the destination before removing the source, so an unlocked reader can throw task_lifecycle_duplicate_identity
description: Found in the independent Opus review of #793 (QCLI-583), pre-existing and NOT widened or fixed by #793. applyLifecycle (src/application/tasks/local-task-repository.ts:253-275) writes every change destination first and removes the source records only afterwards. A reader that does not hold the lock can therefore list a record in BOTH locations (e.g. tasks/ and completed/) mid-lifecycle, and the duplicate check around :405-409 throws task_lifecycle_duplicate_identity with no repeat scan to absorb it. #793 repeats the scan once only when a listed file vanished (ENOENT); this window raises a duplicate-identity error instead, so it is not covered. Relation to QCLI-582: that task stays open; #793 was shown not to be the fix for its T-1 symptom (edits rename over the destination, so readFile never gets ENOENT), and this is a different window, not a claimed cause of T-1.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An unlocked reader running concurrently with a lifecycle move (complete, archive, demote, close) never observes task_lifecycle_duplicate_identity for a record whose move is in progress, shown by a test that fails against the current write order

The chosen ordering (or a bounded repeat of the duplicate check) is stated and justified in the task notes, including what a crash between the two steps leaves on disk and that recoverLifecycle still repairs it
QCLI-582 is not cited as closed by this task unless a measurement ties T-1 to this window
